title: How to Optimize NVFP4 Attention on NVIDIA RTX Blackwell Through Register Recycling | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA shows how splitting SageAttention3's N128 score tile into two N64 register slots and recycling registers after NVFP4 quantization overlaps next-tile QK with current-tile softmax/PV on register-constrained RTX Blackwell (SM120), yielding up to 1.64x kernel speedup. Reactor's production deployment cut world-model end-to-end latency by up to 15.34%, and the optimization is merged into FlashInfer.

themes.theme: RTX vs data center attention bottlenecks

insights.claim: On NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) GPUs, BF16 attention for video generation models is primarily MMA-bound, whereas on Blackwell data center GPUs softmax is the major bottleneck in forward attention.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Workstation/edge Blackwell parts need different kernel optimizations than data center parts; software leverage differs by SKU.
insights.quote: the NVIDIA RTX Blackwell is bounded by MMA on BF16 Attention

insights.claim: NVIDIA RTX Blackwell has lower BF16 matmul throughput than the data center Blackwell variants, so moving attention to NVFP4 (higher TFLOP/s) is the lever to improve throughput on RTX parts.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: NVFP4 low-precision formats are key to making cheaper RTX Blackwell cards viable for world-model inference.
insights.quote: NVIDIA RTX Blackwell has lower BF16 matmul throughput compared to the data center variants.

insights.claim: FlashAttention3 and FlashAttention4 pipelines that overlap MMA with softmax on Hopper and Blackwell data center GPUs cannot be applied directly to the RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) because it uses a different Tensor Core architecture.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Kernel ecosystems fragment across NVIDIA SKUs; RTX-specific kernels are an open optimization gap.

insights.claim: FlashAttention4 attempts to solve the softmax bottleneck on data center Blackwell through pipelining and exp2 emulation.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Softmax, not matmul, is the limiting factor on top-end data center GPUs.

insights.claim: SageAttention3 is a native NVFP4 attention mechanism for RTX Blackwell SM120 that performs both QK and PV matmuls in NVFP4, with its primary innovation being two-level scaling of the softmax probability matrix P.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: 4-bit attention with accuracy safeguards is moving into practical inference stacks.
insights.locator: How SageAttention3 accelerates attention using NVFP4

insights.claim: Because softmax outputs are confined to [0, 1], they underutilize NVFP4 dynamic range and degrade accuracy; two-level scaling first normalizes values to use the full range before quantizing.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Accuracy risk in FP4 attention is addressable by scaling tricks, supporting wider FP4 adoption.

insights.claim: The original SageAttention3 CTA executes QK, softmax/quantization and PV strictly serially per N128 tile with four producer and eight consumer warps, leaving large gaps in Tensor Core activity during softmax, scaling and quantization.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Idle Tensor Cores signal headroom that pure software scheduling can unlock on existing hardware.
insights.quote: There is a large gap in MMA activity, as there is no compute scheduled on the tensor cores.
insights.locator: This means that the operations within the stable loop

insights.claim: RTX Blackwell's OMMA NVFP4 instruction is constrained to m16n8k64, so covering k=128 requires two synchronous MMA instructions, and TMA loads are bound to 128x128 shapes.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Hardware ISA constraints dictate kernel design; explains why generic kernels underperform on SM120.
insights.locator: Second, the NVIDIA Blackwell RTX OMMA operation

insights.claim: In SageAttention3, producer and consumer warps together use 62,464 registers, about 95.3% of the SM's register capacity, leaving little room for a second score tile buffer.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Register pressure is the binding constraint, which is why a reuse scheme rather than double-buffering was needed.
insights.quote: The total of 62,464 registers occupies approximately 95.3% of the SM’s register capacity.

insights.claim: The optimized kernel splits each N128 score tile into two N64 register slots and reuses a slot's registers for the next tile's QK as soon as that half has been exponentiated and quantized to NVFP4, overlapping next-tile QK with current-tile softmax and PV without a second full score buffer.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: A reusable technique for squeezing more utilization from register-limited GPUs.

insights.claim: On an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96 GB), the optimized NVFP4 attention kernel cut core latency by 1.17x to 1.64x versus the original, with the best case on a synthetic 8,192-token causal workload (0.76466 ms to 0.46659 ms) and 1.18-1.19x on the real LongLive 7,040-token input.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Meaningful software-only gains on shipping hardware raise effective inference capacity per card.

insights.claim: Reactor's production deployment of the NVFP4 attention kernel cut end-to-end inference latency by about 15% for OmniDreams (e.g. 155.92 s to 132.00 s, 15.34% on a 2,045-frame moving run) and about 6.5-6.7% for LongLive.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Attention-heavy world models gain most; real customer traffic validates production readiness.

insights.claim: End-to-end gains were small for Helios (about 1.1-1.8%) and Cosmos 3 Nano policy action prediction (1.70%), showing that kernel-level attention speedups translate unevenly depending on how much of a model's path uses NVFP4 attention.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Don't extrapolate 1.6x kernel wins to whole-model speedups; benefits are workload-dependent.

insights.claim: Reactor, a platform providing low-latency infrastructure and APIs for real-time video, robotics and world models, runs the optimized NVFP4 attention kernel in its production serving stack for real customer traffic.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Signals third-party world-model serving on RTX Blackwell hardware, a demand vector beyond hyperscale data centers.

insights.claim: The core register-recycling NVFP4 attention optimization has been merged into the FlashInfer main branch, exposing an SM120 NVFP4 attention API for broader adoption.
insights.speaker: Atharva Joshi
insights.so_what: Upstreaming into open inference libraries accelerates FP4 adoption and strengthens the NVIDIA software moat.
insights.quote: The core optimization has been merged into the FlashInfer main branch.
